known_answer: Of the three waivers in waivers.json, exactly ONE has an owner. A waiver without an owner is not a decision anybody made -- it is a rule that was switched off and left that way, and it will outlive everyone who remembers why.

cases.why: 'tapeout-review-pending' is a state, not a party. Nobody can be asked about it and nobody is accountable if it is wrong. A presence check on the `approver` key accepts this, which is exactly why the check must be on the VALUE.

cases.form: named party with a ticket and an expiry
cases.why: The control. A gate that rejects this is over-strict, and an over-strict gate gets disabled.

why_rc_is_1_and_not_2: An unowned waiver is not 'I could not check'. The waiver file was read and understood; the finding is that the waiver is invalid. That is a REFUSAL about the submission, so rc=1 under contract §1. rc=2 is for the case where waivers.json could not be read at all -- see the vacuous fixture.

must_not.forbidden: accepting id 36 because the `approver` key exists
must_not.why: the key is present and empty of meaning; check the value, not the key
a gate that cannot be satisfied is a gate that gets removed
